title: Notice of Violation and Hearing for Enforcement of Covenants
text:
LAKEWOOD HOMES HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC.
1234 Oakwood Lane, Suite 100
Austin, Texas 78701

NOTICE OF VIOLATION AND HEARING FOR ENFORCEMENT OF COVENANTS

Cause No. 2024-06789

TO: Mr. Thomas R. Whitfield
2468 Cedar Bend Drive
Austin, Texas 78746

Dear Mr. Whitfield:

This letter serves as formal notice that you are in violation of the Lakewood Homes Homeowners Association Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (the “Declaration”) recorded in the Real Property Records of Travis County, Texas. Specifically, you have failed to maintain the exterior of your residence at 2468 Cedar Bend Drive, resulting in peeling paint, overgrown landscaping, and a non-operational vehicle stored in the driveway for more than 30 consecutive days.

Pursuant to Article V, Section 3.2 of the Declaration, the Association has the right to enforce compliance. Tex. Prop. Code Ann. § 202.004 (West 2023) provides: “A property owners’ association may enforce its dedicatory instruments, including by imposing fines, suspending membership privileges, or seeking injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction.”

The Association’s Board of Directors, through its legal counsel, Greer & Kennerly, PLLC, has authorized this enforcement action. You are hereby ordered to:
1. Repaint all exterior surfaces with approved colors (see attached color chart) within 30 days.
2. Remove all weeds and trim all shrubs to a height not exceeding 12 inches within 14 days.
3. Remove the 2008 Ford F-150, license plate ABC-1234, from the driveway within 7 days.

Failure to comply may result in the imposition of fines of $100 per day, per violation, and legal action, including foreclosure of the Association’s assessment lien. A hearing will be held on January 21, 2025, at 10:00 a.m. at the Association’s office to allow you to present evidence of compliance or show cause why enforcement should not proceed.

If you wish to contest this notice, you must notify the Association in writing within 10 days. You may be represented by counsel. The Association has retained Jennifer L. Morales, Esq. (State Bar No. 24098765), of Greer & Kennerly, PLLC, 500 Congress Avenue, Suite 1500, Austin, Texas 78701, Phone: 512-555-0198, Email: jmorales@greerkennerly.com. All correspondence should be directed to Ms. Morales.

Please also note that the Association recently obtained a judgment in a related matter, Lakewood Homes HOA v. Bentley, 789 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. App.—Austin 2023), which upheld the Association’s authority to impose fines without prior judicial approval. Additionally, the Texas Supreme Court in In re Lakewood Homes HOA, 654 S.W.3d 321 (Tex. 2024), affirmed that self-help remedies are available under the Declaration.

The Board of Directors includes the following individuals:
- Patricia A. Nguyen, President (patricia.nguyen@lakewoodhoa.org)
- Robert J. Kowalski, Vice President (rkowalski@lakewoodhoa.org)
- Sheila M. O’Connor, Secretary (soconnor@lakewoodhoa.org)

Any questions may be directed to the Board’s designated agent, Mr. Kowalski, at 512-555-0199.

Sincerely,

Lakewood Homes Homeowners Association, Inc.
By: Patricia A. Nguyen, President

title: Notice of Lien Foreclosure and Enforcement of Covenants
text:
CEDAR PARK ESTATES HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC.
789 Pecan Street, Suite 200
Cedar Park, Texas 78613

NOTICE OF LIEN FORECLOSURE AND ENFORCEMENT OF COVENANTS

Cause No. 24-0987-CV

TO: Ms. Emily J. Stanton
456 Elm Street, Lot 12
Cedar Park, Texas 78613

Dear Ms. Stanton:

This is an official notice that you are in default of your obligations under the Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions for Cedar Park Estates (“Declaration”). Specifically, you have installed a fence that exceeds the maximum height of four feet, in violation of Section 7.2 of the Declaration. Additionally, you have failed to pay assessments totaling $2,850.00, including late fees and interest, for the period of January 2024 through November 2024.

The Association, acting through its Board, has voted to initiate foreclosure proceedings on the lien securing said assessments. Tex. Prop. Code Ann. § 209.006 (West 2023) states: “A property owners’ association may foreclose a lien for unpaid assessments only after providing notice and an opportunity for a hearing in accordance with this section.” The Association has complied with all notice requirements to date.

You are hereby given 30 days to cure the defaults. If you fail to do so, the Association will proceed with a nonjudicial foreclosure sale. The sale will be conducted by the substitute trustee, Mark A. Reynolds, Esq., of Reynolds & Associates, PLLC, 1000 Main Street, Cedar Park, Texas 78613, Phone: 512-555-0303, Email: mreynolds@reynoldspllc.com.

You have the right to contest this notice by filing a written response with the Association within 15 days. You may also seek legal representation. The Association’s counsel in this matter is David Chen, Esq. (State Bar No. 09876543), of Chen & Hart, LLP, 2000 Lakeshore Drive, Austin, Texas 78701, Phone: 512-555-0404, Email: dchen@chenhart.com. You may contact Mr. Chen directly with any questions.

In support of its position, the Association cites Cedar Park Estates HOA v. Fletcher, 456 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. App.—Austin 2022), which held that fence height restrictions in residential subdivisions are enforceable as written. See also In re Cedar Park Estates HOA, 321 S.W.3d 654 (Tex. 2023) (upholding the Association’s lien priority).

The following individuals serve on the Board of Directors:
- Caroline M. Wright, President (caroline.wright@cpehoa.org)
- Jonathan S. Patel, Treasurer (jpatel@cpehoa.org)
- Linda K. Brooks, Secretary (lbrooks@cpehoa.org)

Please direct all correspondence to Ms. Brooks at the Association’s address or via email.

Sincerely,

Cedar Park Estates Homeowners Association, Inc.
By: Caroline M. Wright, President

title: Notice of Fine and Suspension of Privileges
text:
OAK HILLS CONDOMINIUM ASSOCIATION, INC.
5000 Hilltop Drive, Suite B
Austin, Texas 78731

NOTICE OF FINE AND SUSPENSION OF PRIVILEGES

Cause No. 24-F-5678

TO: Mr. Kevin D. Myers
1200 Towering Oaks, Unit 204
Austin, Texas 78731

Dear Mr. Myers:

This letter constitutes formal notice that you have violated Section 9.1 of the Oak Hills Condominium Bylaws by operating a home-based automotive repair business out of your unit, causing excessive noise, odors, and traffic in the common areas. Additionally, you have failed to comply with a prior warning letter dated October 1, 2024.

Pursuant to Tex. Prop. Code Ann. § 204.010 (West 2023), which provides: “A condominium association may impose reasonable fines for violations of the declaration or bylaws, and may suspend a unit owner’s rights to use common amenities for nonpayment of fines or assessments,” the Board has voted to impose a fine of $500 per week until the business ceases. Furthermore, your access to the pool and fitness center is suspended effective immediately.

You may request a hearing before the Board to contest these actions. The hearing will be scheduled within 15 days of your written request. The Board’s legal counsel is Margaret S. Torres, Esq. (State Bar No. 45678901), of Torres & Klein, P.C., 800 Brazos Street, Suite 300, Austin, Texas 78701, Phone: 512-555-0606, Email: mtorres@torresklein.com. Ms. Torres will represent the Association in any subsequent legal proceedings.

In support of its authority, the Board cites Oak Hills Condo Ass’n v. Nguyen, 654 S.W.3d 123 (Tex. App.—Austin 2023), which upheld a similar fine for a home-based business violating quiet enjoyment. See also In re Oak Hills Condo Ass’n, 789 S.W.3d 456 (Tex. 2024) (reaffirming suspension of amenities as a valid enforcement tool).

The Board of Directors consists of:
- Richard T. Coleman, President (rcoleman@oakhillscondo.org)
- Anita R. Singh, Vice President (asingh@oakhillscondo.org)
- Mark S. Johnson, Treasurer (mjohnson@oakhillscondo.org)
- Laura P. Davis, Secretary (ldavis@oakhillscondo.org)

Please address any correspondence to the Secretary, Ms. Davis, at the Association’s address.

Sincerely,

Oak Hills Condominium Association, Inc.

title: Notice of Special Assessment and Enforcement Action
text:
WILDWOOD MEADOWS HOMEOWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC.
2500 Meadow Lane, Suite 50
Round Rock, Texas 78664

NOTICE OF SPECIAL ASSESSMENT AND ENFORCEMENT ACTION

Cause No. 24-1155-A

TO: Ms. Sarah L. Peterson
78 Wildflower Circle, Lot 45
Round Rock, Texas 78664

Dear Ms. Peterson:

This notice is to inform you that the Board of Directors of Wildwood Meadows Homeowners Association has levied a special assessment of $1,200.00 per lot, payable in full on or before March 1, 2025, for the purpose of repairing the community swimming pool and clubhouse. The assessment was approved by a majority vote of the Board on December 5, 2024, pursuant to Article III, Section 4.1 of the Declaration.

Furthermore, you are in violation of the Declaration by maintaining a storage shed that exceeds the maximum allowed size of 100 square feet, as measured by the exterior dimensions. Your shed measures approximately 144 square feet. You are required to either remove the shed or obtain a variance from the Architectural Review Committee within 30 days.

Tex. Prop. Code Ann. § 203.003 (West 2023) provides: “A homeowners association may adopt and enforce architectural standards, including size limitations, for improvements within the subdivision.” The Association’s Architectural Review Committee has the authority to grant variances upon a showing of hardship, but no such request has been submitted by you.

If you fail to cure the violation or pay the special assessment, the Association will turn the matter over to its legal counsel, Brian T. Henderson, Esq. (State Bar No. 32109876), of Henderson & Walsh, LLP, 1500 Congress Avenue, Suite 2000, Austin, Texas 78701, Phone: 512-555-0808, Email: bhenderson@hendersonwalsh.com. Mr. Henderson will initiate legal proceedings to enforce compliance and collect the assessment.

In support, the Association relies on Wildwood Meadows HOA v. Torres, 123 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. App.—Austin 2021), which held that special assessments for capital improvements are enforceable if approved by the Board. Additionally, In re Wildwood Meadows HOA, 987 S.W.3d 654 (Tex. 2024), confirmed that the Association may impose fines for continued noncompliance with architectural standards.

The Board of Directors includes:
- Gregory M. Foster, President (gfoster@wildwoodhoa.org)
- Cynthia L. Adams, Vice President (cadams@wildwoodhoa.org)
- Robert E. Kim, Treasurer (rkim@wildwoodhoa.org)
- Donna J. White, Secretary (dwhite@wildwoodhoa.org)

All communications should be directed to the Secretary, Ms. White, at the Association’s address.

Sincerely,

Wildwood Meadows Homeowners Association, Inc.
By: Gregory M. Foster, President

title: Notice of Covenant Violation and Mediation Demand
text:
SUGAR CREEK RANCH PROPERTY OWNERS ASSOCIATION, INC.
3500 River Road, Suite 300
Georgetown, Texas 78628

NOTICE OF COVENANT VIOLATION AND MEDIATION DEMAND

Cause No. 24-M-4321

TO: Mr. Jonathan M. Hayes
890 Creek Crossing, Lot 22
Georgetown, Texas 78628

Dear Mr. Hayes:

This notice is sent to inform you that you are in violation of the Sugar Creek Ranch Declaration of Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions (“Declaration”) for the following reasons:
1. You have constructed a fence along the rear property line that encroaches onto the common area greenbelt by approximately three feet.
2. You have stored a recreational vehicle (RV) in the front yard for more than 48 hours, in contravention of Section 5.1 of the Declaration, which prohibits storage of vehicles over 20 feet in length in front of the building line.
3. You have failed to maintain the lawn and landscaping, allowing weeds to exceed 12 inches in height.

Pursuant to Tex. Prop. Code Ann. § 206.001 (West 2023), which reads: “A property owners’ association may require mediation before filing a lawsuit to enforce a restrictive covenant,” the Association hereby demands that you participate in mediation within 30 days to resolve these issues. The mediator will be chosen from the list maintained by the Travis County Dispute Resolution Center.

The Association is represented by counsel: Amanda R. Foster, Esq. (State Bar No. 56789012), of Foster & Associates, PLLC, 2200 Colorado Street, Austin, Texas 78701, Phone: 512-555-1010, Email: afoster@fosterpllc.com. Ms. Foster will attend the mediation on behalf of the Association.

You are also advised that the Association recently prevailed in a similar enforcement action. See Sugar Creek Ranch POA v. Martinez, 456 S.W.3d 789 (Tex. App.—Austin 2023) (upholding the Association’s right to enforce front-yard parking restrictions). Additionally, the Texas Supreme Court in In re Sugar Creek Ranch POA, 654 S.W.3d 321 (Tex. 2024), affirmed that encroachments onto common areas may be ordered removed at the owner’s expense.

The Board of Directors comprises:
- Steven T. Garcia, President (sgarcia@sugarcreekpoa.org)
- Michelle L. Turner, Vice President (mturner@sugarcreekpoa.org)
- James R. Collins, Secretary (jcollins@sugarcreekpoa.org)

Sincerely,

Sugar Creek Ranch Property Owners Association, Inc.
